api.notes: Accessible name of the group, applied through ElementInternals (aria-label). A host aria-label attribute wins.
Cascade: explicit, then an enclosing size provider, then md. The resolved size is provided to every member through sizeContext and buttonGroupContext.

api.reason: A-ref: the host element is the reference; the layout box is exposed as ::part(group).
A-xstyle: use class/style, ::part(group) and custom properties.
A-xstyle: attributes on the host element pass through natively.

hooks.notes: The group answers each requesting member with that member's own position (first, middle, last, only), orientation, resolved size and the group's disabled state.

keyboard.action: Enters the group at the member that last had focus (the first enabled member at first); the next Tab leaves the group
keyboard.when: the group is one tab stop

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the next enabled member, wrapping after the last
Moves focus to the previous enabled member, wrapping before the first
Moves focus to the next enabled member of a vertical group
Moves focus to the previous enabled member of a vertical group
Moves focus to the first enabled member
Moves focus to the last enabled member

keyboard.keys: Arrow keys inside a member's layer
keyboard.action: Stay with that layer (an open menu); the group does not move focus

differences.text: Members are light-DOM children. Each member asks for buttonGroupContext and receives its own position, so first, middle and last corners never depend on :last-child (upstream #2508: a tooltip or menu surface rendered beside a member broke the trailing edge). Corner squaring itself is done by the member with per-corner logical radii (RTL and vertical safe).

The group semantics are set through ElementInternals (role=group, aria-label, aria-disabled) rather than attributes on a wrapper div; a host aria-label attribute overrides the label property. Upstream also exposes data-orientation, which is the reflected orientation attribute here.

Tecton draws primary and secondary groups as one continuous fill with a hairline between segments, tertiary as free-standing rules, outlined as one shared border. That is the members' job (they read position and orientation); the group paints nothing except the elevation shadow.

core.button-group.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] (group semantics through ElementInternals, no cross-root IDREFs) [mwg:accessibility] (roving tabindex composite, single tab stop) [mwg:spatial-navigation] (arrow keys only inside the composite, native scrolling untouched).
